previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease Hb-SS, a history of hepatitis C, and prior osteosarcoma presented with a painful crisis characterized by band-like lower abdominal and left hip pain. She was treated with IV fluids and IV hydromorphone initially, transitioning to oral pain medication as her symptoms improved. Her hemoglobin dropped from 8.8 to 6.9 g/dL, but she declined transfusion due to prior transfusion-related hepatitis C; her levels stabilized at 7.1 g/dL with evidence of reticulocytosis. She remained afebrile without respiratory symptoms. A chest X-ray showed mild pulmonary edema and cardiac enlargement but no acute infection or acute chest syndrome. Hypotension was managed by holding lisinopril temporarily, later restarted at discharge. She was discharged home with stable pain control, instructions to stay hydrated, and follow-up plans with her hematologist and PCP.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with sickle cell crisis// r/o pna

TECHNIQUE:  Single frontal view of the chest

COMPARISON:  ___

FINDINGS: 

No focal consolidation is seen.  Again, there is mild engorgement of the
pulmonary vessels.  No pleural effusion is seen.  There is no evidence of
pneumothorax.  The cardiac mediastinal silhouettes are stable.  Heterogeneous
appearance of the bones is again seen, including sclerosis at the left humeral
head, in this patient with sickle cell.

IMPRESSION: 

Mild engorgement of the pulmonary vessels similar to slightly decreased
compared to the prior study.  No focal consolidation.

EXAMINATION:  MR HIP ___ CONRAST RIGHT

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with sickle cell disease, R hip pain// r/o
avascular necrosis, other hip pathology causing pain

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar images of the the right hip were performed without the
administration of intravenous contrast using a hip MR protocol.

COMPARISON:  PET-CT ___.

FINDINGS: 

Bones: Diffuse low T1 bone marrow signal abnormality is consistent with
patient's history of sickle cell disease.  Likely H-shaped deformities of the
lumbar vertebral bodies, not well visualized on this exam.

Serpiginous low T1 and STIR signal within the bilateral posterior iliac bones
is consistent with chronic/healed AVN as there is no STIR signal abnormality
to suggest ongoing infarction.

There is serpiginous low T1 and STIR signal along the subchondral portions of
bilateral femoral heads with some scattered areas of STIR hyperintensity
consistent with AVN.  Cartilage of the left hip appears relatively well
preserved on large field-of-view images.

Right hip: In the anterior right femoral head, among the more chronic changes
of AVN, there is a small subchondral curvilinear focus of subchondral STIR and
PD hyperintensity, measuring 1.5 cm anterior to posterior but only 2 to 3 mm
in width (image 7:20), which may represent a small component of more active
infarction versus subchondral insufficiency fracturing/impending collapse of
the right femoral head.  There is no current collapse of the femoral head.

Cartilage appears relatively well preserved.  No displaced labral tear is
identified on these non arthrographic images.  Small amount of fluid extending
along the chondral labral junction of the superior labrum and posteriorly
likely represents small amount of fluid within sulcus.

Soft tissues: There is moderate amount of edema posterior to the right
proximal femur near the insertion of the gluteus maximus tendon which likely
represents strain and/or partial tearing.  Bilateral hamstring insertions
appear relatively on remarkable.  Bilateral iliopsoas tendons appear
relatively unremarkable.  Bilateral rectus femoris proximal insertions appear
unremarkable.  Muscle bulk about the hip appears preserved.

Multiple mildly prominent inguinal lymph nodes are partially visualized on
coronal images.  The largest measures up to 1.1 cm in short axis on the right.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Findings consistent with avascular necrosis of the bilateral femoral
heads.  No definite collapse is identified, however small area of subchondral
curvilinear STIR signal along the anterior right femoral head may represent a
small focus of more active infarction or small area of subchondral
insufficiency fracturing/impending collapse.
2.  Moderate amount of edema along the posterior aspect of the right proximal
femur near the insertion of gluteus maximus likely represents strain with or
without a component of partial tearing.
3.  Mildly prominent bilateral inguinal lymph nodes are partially imaged and
may be reactive.  Clinical and possible imaging follow-up a is recommended
given patient's prior history of sarcoma.
4.  Diffuse bone marrow abnormality is consistent with patient's sickle cell
disease.
5.  Likely chronic AVN of the bilateral posterior iliac bones.
